thread:
Ava (oncall): @channel quick heads-up — since 16:12 we've seen an uptick of 502/504s and p95 timeouts for hosted inference in us-east-1. Customers reporting API timeouts and failed streams. Opening rapid-response thread.
Miguel (sre): Can you drop an example request_id and the route? I'll pull traces.
Priya (support): Ticket from ACME Corp — request_id=rid-9f3a. They hit streaming endpoint /v1/chat/stream and got 504 after 30s. Posting curl they used:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"rwx-large","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream -v
```
Ava (oncall): here's a live snippet from gateway logs around rid-9f3a — lots of upstream 502s and backend 504s, connection resets: 
```
16:13:02 gateway[proxy-3]: upstream returned 502 for route /v1/chat/stream req=rid-9f3a node=host-47
16:13:05 runtime[worker-12]: kvcache miss for key model-rwx-large-kv user=acme corp
16:13:07 gateway[proxy-3]: upstream timeout after 30s for req=rid-9f3a
```
Jordan (runtime): I see a sudden spike in KV cache misses and batch queue depth on the hosted pool. Also a config push to kv-cache params completed at 16:10. Suspect the config caused evictions and cold-start latency.
deploy-bot: deploy "kv-cache-config-v2" completed at 16:10 by jordan; status=success
Miguel (sre): Autoscaler metrics: GPU utilization normal, but proxy connection count doubled and half-open sockets increased. Could be rate of new sessions + cold KV. Grabbing trace samples now.
Priya (support): Multiple customers (ACME, BetaApps) report streaming timeouts and 502s. Shared support note to affected accounts; asking for any workaround we can offer (fallback route?).
Ava (oncall): Mitigations applied: 1) rolled back kv-cache-config to previous at 16:20 (rollback initiated). 2) Enabled circuit-breaker fallback to smaller prewarmed model pool for enterprise accounts (manual route override). 3) Temporarily throttled low-priority anonymous routes to protect capacity. Monitoring p95 and error-rate.
Jordan (runtime): KV cache warmup in progress after rollback; batch queue depth falling. p95 latency improved from 2.4s to 1.1s over 8 minutes. I recommend postmortem + action items: add canary to kv-cache config, prewarm on deploy, add particle-level alert for kv miss rate > 5% and queue depth > X.
Miguel (sre): Added temporary dashboard panels and increased log retention for the 16:10-16:30 window. I'll owner the follow-up to correlate proxy half-open sockets with client patterns.
Priya (support): Sent initial status update to affected customers at 16:28: "We're aware of intermittent 502/504s and have applied mitigations; we're investigating root cause and will follow up with a timeline."
Ava (oncall): Closing rapid-response phase at 16:35 — error rates back near baseline but keeping an eye on regressions. Action items (owners):
- Jordan: run postmortem on kv-cache-config change, include prewarm checklist and canary plan (due EOD).
- Miguel: correlate proxy connection patterns, add alerting for half-open socket surge (due tomorrow).
- Priya: prepare customer communication template for postmortem with expected timeline (due tomorrow morning).
- Ava: add rollback playbook entries for future KV cache changes and ensure oncall knows the manual fallback route (due EOD).
ops-bot: incident-severity set to P2 by Ava at 16:29
Miguel (sre): noted a likely short-term prevention: add a 2-minute smoothing window before applying KV cache eviction thresholds on busy pools.
Jordan (runtime): +1 for canary + auto-prewarm. I'll draft infra PR and link to postmortem.
Ava (oncall): Thanks all — will file the incident POSTMORTEM and tag owners. If anyone spots a regression ping here immediately. :thumbsup:
